per_question.question: Is there a maximum earned income limit for people on HCWD (Health Coverage for Workers with Disabilities), and what premiums apply?
per_question.agent_answer:
Yes. Under HCWD, **there is not a maximum total earned/countable income limit that makes someone ineligible solely because earnings are too high**. Instead, HCWD uses **cost-sharing that rises with income**. The important income cutoff for eligibility is different: **a person with unearned income over 150% of FPL is not eligible for HCWD**. [MA-2180 HEALTH COVERAGE FOR WORKERS WITH DISABILITIES](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma-2180-3.pdf); [CHANGE NOTICE FOR MANUAL NO. 01-14, HCWD Phase III](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma_cn01-14.pdf)

## Income limit

HCWD eligibility generally requires the person to meet the program’s income rules, but the HCWD policy change notice specifically says HCWD was revised **“to state that HCWD covers individuals regardless of total countable income”** and **“to remove limits on countable income except for the 150% of Federal Poverty Level (FPL) cap on unearned income and provide information about sliding scale premiums.”** [CHANGE NOTICE FOR MANUAL NO. 01-14, HCWD Phase III](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma_cn01-14.pdf)

The current MA-2180 income section states:

- **Unearned income over 150% FPL:** not eligible for HCWD.
- **Total countable income at or below 150% FPL:** no cost-sharing other than applicable copays.
- **Total countable income over 150% FPL:** $50 annual enrollment fee.
- **Total countable monthly income over 200% FPL:** monthly premium in addition to the enrollment fee.
- Premiums increase with income, and once income is **over 450% FPL**, the person pays a **full premium**. [MA-2180 HEALTH COVERAGE FOR WORKERS WITH DISABILITIES](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma-2180-3.pdf)

So, if by “maximum earned income limit” you mean a ceiling on wages/earned income for HCWD eligibility, **the retrieved policy does not show a hard earned-income cutoff**. Instead, higher income leads to an enrollment fee and then higher monthly premiums. The policy does **not** say a person becomes ineligible just because earned income exceeds a set maximum. [CHANGE NOTICE FOR MANUAL NO. 01-14, HCWD Phase III](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma_cn01-14.pdf); [MA-2180 HEALTH COVERAGE FOR WORKERS WITH DISABILITIES](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma-2180-3.pdf)

## Premiums that apply

The MA-2180 premium chart in the base HCWD manual has been amended; the current amendment says **“MA-2180.IV.I - HCWD Premiums Income chart has been updated.”** effective **January 1, 2025**. The change notice confirms the chart was updated, but the retrieved amendment text does **not include the new dollar figures**. [CHANGE NOTICE FOR MANUAL NO. 03-25, 2025 Federal Poverty Level Changes (FPL) Income Changes](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/CN-NO-03-25.docx.pdf)

From the HCWD manual text I was able to verify, the premium structure is:

- **0–150% FPL:** $0 monthly premium
- **151–200% FPL:** $0 monthly premium
- **201–250% FPL:** $196 individual / $265 couple
- **251–300% FPL:** $235 individual / $318 couple
- **301–350% FPL:** $274 individual / $370 couple
- **351–400% FPL:** $313 individual / $423 couple
- **401–450% FPL:** $352 individual / $476 couple
- **451% FPL and above:** **$875** full premium for both individual and couple [MA-2180 HEALTH COVERAGE FOR WORKERS WITH DISABILITIES](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma-2180-3.pdf)

## Important caution on the dollar ranges

I can verify that the **premium amounts** above appear in MA-2180, but I **cannot confirm from the retrieved materials that the income-dollar ranges in that chart are still current**, because the 2025 change notice says the HCWD premium income chart was updated. So the safest reading is:

- the **structure** remains:
  - no premium through 200% FPL,
  - $50 annual enrollment fee above 150% FPL,
  - monthly premium above 200% FPL,
  - full premium above 450% FPL;
- but the **exact monthly income bracket dollar thresholds** should be taken from the **current post-2025 HCWD premium chart**. [CHANGE NOTICE FOR MANUAL NO. 03-25, 2025 Federal Poverty Level Changes (FPL) Income Changes](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/CN-NO-03-25.docx.pdf); [MA-2180 HEALTH COVERAGE FOR WORKERS WITH DISABILITIES](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma-2180-3.pdf)

## Bottom line

- **No hard maximum earned income limit** was verified in the retrieved HCWD policy.
- **Unearned income over 150% FPL makes the person ineligible.**
- **Over 150% FPL:** $50 annual enrollment fee.
- **Over 200% FPL:** monthly premium, increasing with income.
- **Over 450% FPL:** full premium. [MA-2180 HEALTH COVERAGE FOR WORKERS WITH DISABILITIES](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma-2180-3.pdf); [CHANGE NOTICE FOR MANUAL NO. 01-14, HCWD Phase III](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/ma_cn01-14.pdf); [CHANGE NOTICE FOR MANUAL NO. 03-25, 2025 Federal Poverty Level Changes (FPL) Income Changes](https://policies.ncdhhs.gov/wp-content/uploads/CN-NO-03-25.docx.pdf)

If you want, I can next help translate this into a practical rule like: “If a client has X wages and Y unearned income, what HCWD charges should they expect?”

scores.explanation: The agent's answer correctly identifies all key facts: no maximum earned income limit, 150% FPL cap only on unearned income, $50 per certification period enrollment fee above 150% FPL, sliding-scale monthly premiums above 200% FPL, and full premium above 450% FPL. These align precisely with the reference answer and evidence sections. The agent provides specific premium figures (e.g., $196/$265 at 201-250% FPL) which are presented as coming from MA-2180 but flagged with an honest caveat that 2025 updates may have changed the dollar thresholds - this is appropriate disclosure rather than hallucination. The slight hallucination deduction is for presenting specific dollar premium amounts as facts from the policy without the [unverified] marker, though the agent does add a cautionary note. Citations are precise, referencing specific policy documents (MA-2180, Change Notice 01-14, Change Notice 03-25) with URLs. The answer is thorough, well-structured, and a Medicaid policy expert would find it accurate and useful.
